{"design":"HOST DECIDED by Mark, 2026-11-22: the host stood up this session IS the
interop-day host. No fresh EC2 instance.

That replaces the plan in the description and notes, and changes three
things materially:

- NAME: mimi.reviewcommit.com, not mimid.reviewcommit.com. This is
  permanent for every room made here: protocol-07 §5.6 puts the hub's
  identity in the roomId, so a room cannot be re-homed. Haven must be
  given this name, and the provider key's TXT record must be published
  under it.
- PLACE: dokr (10.69.44.52, tailnet 100.87.123.117), not EC2. So there
  is no new security group to build and no world-open SSH to avoid;
  SSH is jrluser@10.69.44.52 on the LAN.
- SHAPE: Caddy on joumon (198.71.58.180) terminates TLS and reverse
  proxies to http://100.87.123.117:8084 (joumon
  /etc/caddy/Caddyfile:185). mimid listens on the tailnet, plain.

AUDITED ON THE LIVE HOST, 2026-11-22:

Done.
- mimid and mimid-agent both active, binaries built 2026-11-22 16:00,
  which is after main 677d0d06 (14:29). So the code requirements in the
  description are satisfied by the deployed build: mls-extensions-11,
  the role-1 list rule (1aa8400), nonces (6dbe357), Room/create roomId.
- TLS and a valid public certificate; /.well-known/jmap answers 401.
- domain, base_url, listen, local_listen and database configured;
  [provider_auth] dns_servers = 9.9.9.9, 1.1.1.1.

Missing, and each is needed before an interop day.
1. PROVIDER SIGNING KEY. [provider_auth] carries dns_servers and
   nothing else: no signing key, and no mimid1._mimi TXT record exists
   (checked mimid1._mimi.mimi.reviewcommit.com, _mimi.mimi...,
   mimid1._mimi.reviewcommit.com: all empty). Without it mimid cannot
   sign RFC 9421 requests to Haven and Haven cannot verify us, so this
   gates everything else. Epik must be reached FROM joumon, over IPv4
   (curl -4: the signature is registered to joumon's v4, and it egresses
   v6 by default), key from rbw, and the v2 additive endpoint, never v1
   SetHostRecords, which deletes every record.
2. PKIX mTLS (mimid-75nk.5). No [peer_tls] at all.
3. [trusted_proxy], and this is NO LONGER OPTIONAL. The description
   offered "mimid terminates TLS or Caddy + X-Client-Cert +
   [trusted_proxy]". Choosing this host forecloses the first: Caddy
   terminates TLS on a different machine, so mimid can never see a
   peer's client certificate directly. PKIX mTLS here REQUIRES Caddy
   client_auth on the mimi.reviewcommit.com site block, the certificate
   forwarded as a header, and [trusted_proxy] naming the tailnet hop.
   That is new work on joumon's Caddyfile, not just mimid config.
4. HAVEN PEERING. No peer configured, so no enforce mode and no DNS
   keys. Haven enforcing needs Mark's OK, per the notes.
5. OPENTELEMETRY. No OTEL settings in the unit.
6. mimid-chat. Not installed; only mimid and mimid-agent are. The
   description ties Room/create roomId to deploying a matching
   mimid-chat.

Also true of this host and not of the EC2 plan: the IRC front end is
live on the tailnet (100.87.123.117:6667) and the agent on 127.0.0.1:8486.
One account, mimi://mimi.reviewcommit.com/u/mark, zero rooms.

NO SUB-ISSUES FILED: per AGENTS.md, Mark approves a plan before its
sub-issues exist. Items 1 to 6 above are the proposed plan."}
